ko.title: [물류 101 #10] 양초 한 개를 배송하는 비용이 천 개를 배송하는 것보다 더 드는 이유

segments.src: > The route a product takes to reach you — the distribution channel — decides what kind of warehouse it has to pass through, and that decision drives most of the shipping cost you never see on the price tag.
segments.tr: > 제품이 당신에게 도달하는 경로, 즉 유통 채널은 제품이 어떤 창고를 거쳐야 하는지를 결정하며, 그 결정이 가격표에서는 보이지 않는 배송비의 대부분을 좌우합니다.
## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: A **distribution channel** is simply the path a product travels from the company that makes it to the person who uses it.
segments.tr: **유통 채널**은 제품이 만드는 회사에서 그것을 사용하는 사람에게 도달하는 경로일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: Channels are usually described by how many middle stops they contain:
segments.tr: 유통 채널은 보통 중간에 거치는 단계의 수로 구분합니다:

segments.src: - **Zero-level (direct-to-consumer):** maker → you. A brand's own website.
segments.tr: - **0단계(직접 판매, direct-to-consumer):** 제조사 → 소비자. 브랜드 자체 웹사이트입니다.

segments.src: - **One-level:** maker → retailer → you. A jar of salsa sold at Kroger.
segments.tr: - **1단계:** 제조사 → 소매업체 → 소비자. 크로거(Kroger)에서 판매되는 살사 소스 한 병입니다.

segments.src: - **Two-level:** maker → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you. How most small hardware stores and restaurants get supplied.
segments.tr: - **2단계:** 제조사 → 도매업체/유통업체 → 소매업체 → 소비자. 대부분의 작은 철물점과 식당이 물건을 공급받는 방식입니다.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: the channel isn't just a sales decision.
segments.tr: 여기서 많은 사람이 놀라는 부분이 있습니다. 유통 채널은 단순한 영업 결정이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It quietly dictates your *logistics*, because each channel hands off goods in a different **unit of handling**.
segments.tr: 유통 채널은 조용하지만 *물류*를 결정합니다. 채널마다 상품을 넘기는 **취급 단위**가 다르기 때문입니다.
세 가지 크기를 생각해 보세요:
pallet  →  case  →  each (one single unit)
팔레트 하나에는 상자(케이스) 40개가 실릴 수 있습니다.
케이스 하나에는 양초 12개가 들어갈 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Moving one pallet takes a forklift driver about a minute.
segments.tr: 팔레트 하나를 옮기는 데 지게차 기사는 약 1분이 걸립니다.

segments.src: Picking, packing, labeling, and shipping *one* candle takes a person a few minutes and a box, and then a parcel carrier charges you for a separate delivery to a separate house.
segments.tr: 양초 *한 개*를 피킹하고, 포장하고, 라벨을 붙이고, 출고하는 데는 사람 한 명이 몇 분과 상자 하나가 필요하고, 그다음에는 택배사가 별도의 집으로 가는 별도의 배송 요금을 청구합니다.

segments.src: That's why the cost per unit climbs steeply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 그래서 취급 단위가 작아질수록 개당 비용이 가파르게 올라갑니다.

segments.src: Same product, same warehouse racks — completely different economics.
segments.tr: 같은 제품, 같은 창고 선반이라도 경제성은 완전히 다릅니다.

segments.src: This split shows up in the buildings themselves:
segments.tr: 이러한 차이는 건물 자체에서도 드러납니다:

segments.src: - A **distribution center (DC)** is built for *replenishment*. Trucks arrive with pallets, and trucks leave with pallets and cases headed to stores. Big doors, big equipment, few touches per item. Some DCs barely store anything at all — in **cross-docking**, inbound freight is sorted and reloaded onto outbound trucks within hours.
segments.tr: - **유통센터(distribution center, DC)**는 *보충(replenishment)*을 위해 지어집니다. 트럭이 팔레트를 싣고 도착하고, 팔레트와 케이스를 싣고 매장으로 향하며 떠납니다. 큰 출입문, 큰 장비, 상품당 손길은 적습니다. 일부 DC는 거의 보관을 하지 않습니다. **크로스도킹(cross-docking)**에서는 입고 화물이 분류되어 몇 시간 안에 출고 트럭에 다시 실립니다.

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - **풀필먼트 센터(fulfillment center, FC)**는 *주문*을 위해 지어집니다. 케이스 단위로 입고받지만 수천 개의 개별 주소로 낱개 상품을 출고합니다. 소형 상품을 고밀도로 보관하는 공간, 피킹 동선, 포장 스테이션, 박스 선택, 라벨 프린터, 반품 데스크가 필요합니다. 상품당 손길이 많이 갑니다.

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: **풀필먼트(Fulfillment)**는 주문 측면의 전체 흐름을 가리키는 이름입니다: 입고 → 보관 → 피킹 → 포장 → 출고 → 반품 처리.

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: 기업은 이를 직접 구축하거나 **3PL**(제3자 물류업체, third-party logistics provider)에게 빌려 씁니다. 3PL은 재고를 보관하고 수수료를 받고 주문을 출고해 주는 외부 업체이므로, 창고 임대 계약을 따로 맺을 필요가 없습니다.

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: 오늘날 대부분의 브랜드는 **옴니채널**, 즉 여러 채널을 동시에 운영합니다.

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: 이는 진짜 어려운 문제를 낳습니다. 재고 풀은 하나인데 수요 흐름은 여럿입니다.

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: 마지막 한 개를 웹사이트와 매장에서 동시에 판매하면 누군가의 주문이 취소됩니다.

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: 또한 **매장 출고(ship-from-store, 가장 가까운 매장이 소형 FC 역할을 함)**와 **BOPIS**(온라인 구매 후 매장 픽업, buy online, pick up in store)처럼 영리한 해법도 낳는데, 후자는 비싼 라스트 마일 배송을 고객 자신의 차량 이동으로 넘깁니다.
## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you run a candle company in Portland, Oregon.
segments.tr: 오리건주 포틀랜드에서 양초 회사를 운영한다고 해 봅시다.

segments.src: One product, one factory, three channels.
segments.tr: 제품 하나, 공장 하나, 채널 세 개입니다.

segments.src: Watch what happens to the logistics.
segments.tr: 물류에 어떤 일이 일어나는지 살펴보세요.

segments.src: **Channel 1 — Target.** You sell wholesale at about $6 a unit.
segments.tr: **채널 1 — 타깃(Target).** 개당 약 6달러에 도매로 판매합니다.

segments.src: You palletize, book a truck, and deliver to a Target regional distribution center; Target moves it to stores from there.
segments.tr: 팔레트에 싣고, 트럭을 예약하고, 타깃의 지역 유통센터로 배송하면 타깃이 거기서 매장으로 옮깁니다.

segments.src: Your per-unit logistics cost is pennies to a few dimes, because you touched pallets, not candles.
segments.tr: 양초가 아니라 팔레트를 다루기 때문에 개당 물류비는 몇 센트에서 십 센트 남짓입니다.

segments.src: The trade-off: thin margin, strict delivery windows and labeling rules, and you never learn who the buyer is.
segments.tr: 대가는 얇은 마진, 엄격한 배송 시간대와 라벨 규정이며, 구매자가 누구인지 절대 알 수 없다는 점입니다.

segments.src: **Channel 2 — your own Shopify store.** You sell at $28.
segments.tr: **채널 2 — 자체 Shopify 스토어.** 28달러에 판매합니다.
이제는 *당신이* 풀필먼트 센터입니다.

segments.src: Someone in Cleveland orders one candle.
segments.tr: 클리블랜드에 사는 누군가가 양초 한 개를 주문합니다.
예를 들면 다음과 같습니다:
pick + pack labor      ~$2-3
box + dunnage          ~$1
parcel shipping        ~$8-10  (2 lb, cross-country, residential)
per-order cost         ~$11-14

segments.src: Then add returns and damage — modest for a candle, but in categories like apparel commonly 20–30% of online orders — with each one needing an inspection, a restock, and a refund.
segments.tr: 여기에 반품과 파손이 더해집니다. 양초에서는 많지 않지만, 의류처럼 온라인 주문의 20–30%에 이르는 카테고리도 흔합니다. 반품 건마다 검수, 재입고, 환불이 필요합니다.

segments.src: Great margin on paper, far less after the box leaves.
segments.tr: 장부상으로는 마진이 훌륭하지만, 상자가 출고된 뒤에는 훨씬 줄어듭니다.

segments.src: **Channel 3 — Amazon.** You ship cases to an Amazon FC in, say, Ontario, California, and Amazon picks, packs, and ships each order.
segments.tr: **채널 3 — 아마존(Amazon).** 예를 들어 캘리포니아주 온타리오에 있는 아마존 FC로 케이스를 보내면, 아마존이 주문마다 피킹, 포장, 출고를 합니다.

segments.src: You pay a per-unit fulfillment fee (a few dollars for a small, light item), monthly storage, and a referral fee that's commonly around 15% of the sale price in many categories.
segments.tr: 개당 풀필먼트 수수료(작고 가벼운 상품이면 몇 달러), 월 보관료, 그리고 많은 카테고리에서 흔히 판매가의 약 15%인 판매 수수료를 냅니다.

segments.src: You've rented someone else's fulfillment operation — and inherited their rules about how everything must be boxed, barcoded, and forecast.
segments.tr: 다른 회사의 풀필먼트 운영을 빌려 쓰는 셈이며, 모든 것을 어떻게 박스에 담고, 바코드를 붙이고, 수요를 예측해야 하는지에 대한 그들의 규칙도 함께 물려받습니다.

segments.src: Notice that the candle never changed.
segments.tr: 양초는 전혀 바뀌지 않았다는 점에 주목하세요.

segments.src: The *channel* changed, and the entire logistics design changed with it: truckload vs.
segments.tr: *채널*이 바뀌었고, 물류 설계 전체가 함께 바뀌었습니다: 트럭 단위(truckload) 대
택배(parcel), 팔레트 대
낱개(eaches), 한 번의 배송 대
수천 건의 배송, 반품 데스크 없음 대
바쁜 반품 데스크.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson — and it's why the same brand can be profitable in one channel and quietly lose money in another.
segments.tr: 이것이 이번 수업의 핵심이며, 같은 브랜드가 한 채널에서는 수익을 내면서 다른 채널에서는 조용히 손해를 볼 수 있는 이유입니다.
## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. A distribution channel is the path from maker to end user, and each added level changes who holds inventory and who takes the risk.
segments.tr: 1. 유통 채널은 제조사에서 최종 사용자까지의 경로이며, 단계가 추가될 때마다 재고를 누가 보유하고 위험을 누가 지는지가 달라집니다.

segments.src: 2. Distribution centers move pallets and cases to stores; fulfillment centers pick single units for individual shoppers, so cost per unit rises sharply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 2. 유통센터는 팔레트와 케이스를 매장으로 옮기고, 풀필먼트 센터는 개별 고객을 위해 낱개를 피킹하므로, 취급 단위가 작아질수록 개당 비용이 크게 올라갑니다.

segments.src: 3. Running multiple channels at once (omnichannel) means one inventory pool serving several very different cost structures — which is exactly where profit gets made or lost.
segments.tr: 3. 여러 채널을 동시에 운영하는 것(옴니채널)은 하나의 재고 풀로 매우 다른 여러 비용 구조를 감당한다는 뜻이며, 바로 여기서 이익이 나거나 손실이 발생합니다.
## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A brand sells through a wholesaler, who sells to independent grocery stores, who sell to shoppers.
segments.tr: **1.** 한 브랜드가 도매업체를 통해 판매하고, 도매업체는 독립 식료품점에 팔고, 식료품점은 쇼핑객에게 판매합니다.
이것은 몇 단계 유통 채널입니까?
- A) 0단계
- B) 1단계
- C) 2단계
- D) 옴니채널

segments.src: **2.** True or False — Cross-docking is a strategy for storing inventory longer to protect against demand spikes.
segments.tr: **2.** 참 또는 거짓 — 크로스도킹은 수요 급증에 대비해 재고를 더 오래 보관하는 전략이다.

segments.src: **3.** Which of these would you expect to cost the *most per unit shipped*?
segments.tr: **3.** 다음 중 *출고 단위당 비용이 가장 클 것*으로 예상되는 것은 무엇입니까?

segments.src: - A) Delivering full pallets to a retailer's regional DC
segments.tr: - A) 소매업체의 지역 DC로 팔레트 단위 전체를 배송

segments.src: - B) Shipping cases to a retailer's store
segments.tr: - B) 소매업체 매장으로 케이스 단위 출고

segments.src: - C) Picking and parcel-shipping one item to a customer's home
segments.tr: - C) 상품 한 개를 피킹해 고객 집으로 택배 출고

segments.src: - D) All three cost about the same per unit
segments.tr: - D) 세 가지 모두 개당 비용이 거의 같다
## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The route a product takes from producer to end customer, including any wholesalers, retailers, or marketplaces along the way.
segments.tr: - **유통 채널(Distribution channel)** — 생산자에서 최종 고객까지 제품이 거치는 경로로, 중간의 도매업체, 소매업체, 마켓플레이스를 포함합니다.

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC)** — A facility that receives bulk freight and replenishes stores or other DCs, mostly handling pallets and cases.
segments.tr: - **유통센터(Distribution center, DC)** — 대량 화물을 입고받아 매장이나 다른 DC를 보충하는 시설로, 주로 팔레트와 케이스를 취급합니다.

segments.src: - **Fulfillment center (FC)** — A facility built to pick, pack, and ship individual customer orders, handling single units and returns.
segments.tr: - **풀필먼트 센터(Fulfillment center, FC)** — 개별 고객 주문을 피킹, 포장, 출고하도록 지어진 시설로, 낱개 상품과 반품을 취급합니다.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — Sorting inbound freight straight onto outbound trucks with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **크로스도킹(Cross-docking)** — 중간 보관을 거의 하지 않고 입고 화물을 곧바로 출고 트럭에 분류해 싣는 방식.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics provider)** — An outside company you hire to warehouse inventory and fulfill orders on your behalf.
segments.tr: - **3PL(제3자 물류업체, third-party logistics provider)** — 재고를 보관하고 대신 주문을 처리하도록 고용하는 외부 기업.

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Selling through several channels at once (store, website, marketplace, pickup) while trying to serve them from one inventory pool.
segments.tr: - **옴니채널(Omnichannel)** — 매장, 웹사이트, 마켓플레이스, 픽업 등 여러 채널에서 동시에 판매하면서 하나의 재고 풀로 이들을 처리하려는 방식.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Two middle stops (wholesaler and retailer) between maker and shopper makes it a two-level channel.
segments.tr: *정답: **1 — C.** 제조사와 쇼핑객 사이에 중간 단계 두 곳(도매업체와 소매업체)이 있으므로 2단계 유통 채널입니다.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Cross-docking does the opposite: it minimizes storage by moving freight from inbound to outbound trucks within hours, trading inventory buffer for speed and lower holding cost.
segments.tr: **2 — 거짓.** 크로스도킹은 정반대입니다. 화물을 몇 시간 안에 입고 트럭에서 출고 트럭으로 옮겨 보관을 최소화하며, 재고 완충분을 속도와 낮은 보관 비용으로 맞바꿉니다.

segments.src: **3 — C.** Picking a single unit means the most labor touches per item plus a dedicated parcel delivery to one address, so its cost per unit is far above pallet or case movement.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** 낱개를 피킹하면 상품당 작업 손길이 가장 많고 한 주소로 가는 별도 택배 배송까지 필요하므로, 개당 비용이 팔레트나 케이스 이동보다 훨씬 높습니다.*

zh.title: [物流 101 #10] 为什么运送一支蜡烛的成本，比运送一千支还高

segments.src: > The route a product takes to reach you — the distribution channel — decides what kind of warehouse it has to pass through, and that decision drives most of the shipping cost you never see on the price tag.
segments.tr: > 产品送达你手中的路径——即分销渠道——决定了它必须经过哪种仓库，而这一决定也带来了大部分你在价格标签上看不到的运费。
## 今日概念

segments.src: A **distribution channel** is simply the path a product travels from the company that makes it to the person who uses it.
segments.tr: **分销渠道**指的就是产品从生产企业到最终使用者之间所经过的路径。

segments.src: Channels are usually described by how many middle stops they contain:
segments.tr: 渠道通常按其中间环节的数量来划分：

segments.src: - **Zero-level (direct-to-consumer):** maker → you. A brand's own website.
segments.tr: - **零级渠道（直销）：** 生产商 → 你。即品牌自己的网站。

segments.src: - **One-level:** maker → retailer → you. A jar of salsa sold at Kroger.
segments.tr: - **一级渠道：** 生产商 → 零售商 → 你。例如在 Kroger 超市销售的一罐莎莎酱。

segments.src: - **Two-level:** maker → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you. How most small hardware stores and restaurants get supplied.
segments.tr: - **二级渠道：** 生产商 → 批发商/分销商 → 零售商 → 你。大多数小型五金店和餐厅的进货方式都是如此。

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: the channel isn't just a sales decision.
segments.tr: 让人意外的是：渠道不仅仅是一个销售决策。

segments.src: It quietly dictates your *logistics*, because each channel hands off goods in a different **unit of handling**.
segments.tr: 它还会悄悄决定你的*物流方式*，因为每种渠道交接货物时所用的**处理单位**各不相同。
可以想象三种尺寸：
pallet  →  case  →  each (one single unit)
一个托盘可能装 40 箱。
一箱可能装 12 支蜡烛。

segments.src: Moving one pallet takes a forklift driver about a minute.
segments.tr: 搬运一个托盘，叉车司机大约需要一分钟。

segments.src: Picking, packing, labeling, and shipping *one* candle takes a person a few minutes and a box, and then a parcel carrier charges you for a separate delivery to a separate house.
segments.tr: 拣选、打包、贴标并发运*一支*蜡烛，则需要一个人花几分钟和一个纸箱，之后还要由快递承运商另外收费，将它送到另一户人家。

segments.src: That's why the cost per unit climbs steeply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么处理单位越小，单位成本就越高得惊人。

segments.src: Same product, same warehouse racks — completely different economics.
segments.tr: 同样的产品、同样的仓库货架——经济账却完全不同。

segments.src: This split shows up in the buildings themselves:
segments.tr: 这种区别直接体现在仓库建筑本身上：

segments.src: - A **distribution center (DC)** is built for *replenishment*. Trucks arrive with pallets, and trucks leave with pallets and cases headed to stores. Big doors, big equipment, few touches per item. Some DCs barely store anything at all — in **cross-docking**, inbound freight is sorted and reloaded onto outbound trucks within hours.
segments.tr: - **配送中心（DC）** 是为*补货*而建的。卡车运来的是托盘，运走的是发往门店的托盘和整箱货。大门宽敞，设备庞大，每件商品经手次数少。有些配送中心几乎不储存货物——在**越库作业（cross-docking）**中，入库货物会在数小时内分拣并重新装上出库卡车。

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - **履约中心（FC）** 是为*订单*而建的。它接收整箱货，但要把单件商品发往成千上万个不同地址。它需要高密度的小件存储、拣货路径、打包工位、选箱系统、标签打印机以及退货处理台。每件商品经手次数多。

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: **履约（Fulfillment）** 指的是订单端的整个流程：收货 → 存储 → 拣货 → 打包 → 发运 → 处理退货。

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: 企业要么自建履约体系，要么向**第三方物流（3PL）**租用——即由外部公司为你存放库存、按费用为你发运订单，这样你就无需签订仓库租约。

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: 如今大多数品牌都采用**全渠道（omnichannel）**运营——同时经营多个渠道。

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: 这带来了一个真正棘手的问题：库存只有一个池子，需求却有多个来源。

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: 如果你的官网和门店同时卖出最后一件商品，就会有某个订单被取消。

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: 这也催生了一些巧妙的解决方案，例如**门店发货（ship-from-store）**（最近的门店充当迷你履约中心），以及 **BOPIS**（线上下单、到店自提），后者把昂贵的最后一公里转嫁到了顾客自己的开车出行上。
## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Say you run a candle company in Portland, Oregon.
segments.tr: 假设你在俄勒冈州波特兰经营一家蜡烛公司。

segments.src: One product, one factory, three channels.
segments.tr: 一款产品、一座工厂、三个渠道。

segments.src: Watch what happens to the logistics.
segments.tr: 看看物流会发生什么变化。

segments.src: **Channel 1 — Target.** You sell wholesale at about $6 a unit.
segments.tr: **渠道 1 — Target。** 你以约每件 6 美元的价格批发销售。

segments.src: You palletize, book a truck, and deliver to a Target regional distribution center; Target moves it to stores from there.
segments.tr: 你将货物码成托盘、预约卡车，然后送到 Target 的区域配送中心；再由 Target 从那里配送到各门店。

segments.src: Your per-unit logistics cost is pennies to a few dimes, because you touched pallets, not candles.
segments.tr: 你的单件物流成本只有几分到几毛钱，因为你处理的是托盘，而不是单支蜡烛。

segments.src: The trade-off: thin margin, strict delivery windows and labeling rules, and you never learn who the buyer is.
segments.tr: 代价是：利润率很薄，配送时间和贴标规则都很严格，而且你永远不知道买家是谁。

segments.src: **Channel 2 — your own Shopify store.** You sell at $28.
segments.tr: **渠道 2 — 你自己的 Shopify 店铺。** 你以 28 美元的价格销售。
现在*你*就是履约中心了。

segments.src: Someone in Cleveland orders one candle.
segments.tr: 俄亥俄州克利夫兰的某人下单买了一支蜡烛。
举例来说：
pick + pack labor      ~$2-3
box + dunnage          ~$1
parcel shipping        ~$8-10  (2 lb, cross-country, residential)
per-order cost         ~$11-14

segments.src: Then add returns and damage — modest for a candle, but in categories like apparel commonly 20–30% of online orders — with each one needing an inspection, a restock, and a refund.
segments.tr: 再加上退货和破损——对蜡烛来说不算多，但在服装等品类中，退货通常占线上订单的 20–30%——每一笔都需要检验、重新上架并退款。

segments.src: Great margin on paper, far less after the box leaves.
segments.tr: 纸面上利润率很高，但包裹一旦离开仓库，实际所得就少得多了。

segments.src: **Channel 3 — Amazon.** You ship cases to an Amazon FC in, say, Ontario, California, and Amazon picks, packs, and ships each order.
segments.tr: **渠道 3 — 亚马逊。** 你将整箱货发往位于加利福尼亚州安大略市的一个亚马逊履约中心，由亚马逊为每笔订单拣货、打包并发运。

segments.src: You pay a per-unit fulfillment fee (a few dollars for a small, light item), monthly storage, and a referral fee that's commonly around 15% of the sale price in many categories.
segments.tr: 你需要支付按件计的履约费（小而轻的商品通常为几美元）、月度仓储费，以及在许多品类中通常约为售价 15% 的佣金。

segments.src: You've rented someone else's fulfillment operation — and inherited their rules about how everything must be boxed, barcoded, and forecast.
segments.tr: 你租用了别人的履约体系——同时也接受了他们的规定，即所有商品都必须按要求装箱、贴条码并做好预测。

segments.src: Notice that the candle never changed.
segments.tr: 注意，蜡烛本身始终没有变。

segments.src: The *channel* changed, and the entire logistics design changed with it: truckload vs.
segments.tr: 变的是*渠道*，而整个物流设计也随之改变：整车运输 对比 包裹运输，
托盘 对比 单件，
一次配送 对比 成千上万次配送，
没有退货处理台 对比
退货量很大的处理台。

segments.src: That's the whole lesson — and it's why the same brand can be profitable in one channel and quietly lose money in another.
segments.tr: 这就是全部的道理——也正因为如此，同一个品牌在一个渠道里可以盈利，在另一个渠道里却可能悄无声息地亏损。
## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. A distribution channel is the path from maker to end user, and each added level changes who holds inventory and who takes the risk.
segments.tr: 1. 分销渠道是从生产者到最终用户的路径，每增加一个层级，都会改变由谁持有库存、由谁承担风险。

segments.src: 2. Distribution centers move pallets and cases to stores; fulfillment centers pick single units for individual shoppers, so cost per unit rises sharply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 2. 配送中心向门店输送托盘和整箱货；履约中心则为个人购物者拣选单件商品。处理单位越小，单位成本急剧上升。

segments.src: 3. Running multiple channels at once (omnichannel) means one inventory pool serving several very different cost structures — which is exactly where profit gets made or lost.
segments.tr: 3. 同时运营多个渠道（全渠道）意味着一个库存池要服务于多种差异很大的成本结构——而利润正是在这里被创造或流失的。
## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **1.** A brand sells through a wholesaler, who sells to independent grocery stores, who sell to shoppers.
segments.tr: **1.** 某品牌通过批发商销售，批发商再卖给独立杂货店，杂货店最后卖给购物者。
这属于哪一级渠道？
- A) 零级
- B) 一级
- C) 二级
- D) 全渠道

segments.src: **2.** True or False — Cross-docking is a strategy for storing inventory longer to protect against demand spikes.
segments.tr: **2.** 判断正误——越库作业是一种延长库存存放时间、以应对需求高峰的策略。

segments.src: **3.** Which of these would you expect to cost the *most per unit shipped*?
segments.tr: **3.** 以下哪一种方式的*单件发运成本*最高？

segments.src: - A) Delivering full pallets to a retailer's regional DC
segments.tr: - A) 向零售商的区域配送中心整托盘配送

segments.src: - B) Shipping cases to a retailer's store
segments.tr: - B) 向零售商的门店发运整箱货

segments.src: - C) Picking and parcel-shipping one item to a customer's home
segments.tr: - C) 拣选单件商品并以包裹方式寄送到顾客家中

segments.src: - D) All three cost about the same per unit
segments.tr: - D) 三者单件成本大致相同
## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The route a product takes from producer to end customer, including any wholesalers, retailers, or marketplaces along the way.
segments.tr: - **分销渠道** — 产品从生产者到最终顾客所经过的路径，包括途中的任何批发商、零售商或电商平台。

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC)** — A facility that receives bulk freight and replenishes stores or other DCs, mostly handling pallets and cases.
segments.tr: - **配送中心（DC）** — 接收大批量货物并为门店或其他配送中心补货的设施，主要处理托盘和整箱货。

segments.src: - **Fulfillment center (FC)** — A facility built to pick, pack, and ship individual customer orders, handling single units and returns.
segments.tr: - **履约中心（FC）** — 专为拣选、打包和发运单个客户订单而设计的设施，处理单件商品和退货。

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — Sorting inbound freight straight onto outbound trucks with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **越库作业（Cross-docking）** — 将入库货物直接分拣到出库卡车上，中间很少或无需存储。

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics provider)** — An outside company you hire to warehouse inventory and fulfill orders on your behalf.
segments.tr: - **第三方物流（3PL）** — 你外包给外部公司，由其代为仓储库存并代为履行订单。

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Selling through several channels at once (store, website, marketplace, pickup) while trying to serve them from one inventory pool.
segments.tr: - **全渠道（Omnichannel）** — 同时通过多个渠道（门店、网站、电商平台、自提点）销售，并力求由同一个库存池来供货。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Two middle stops (wholesaler and retailer) between maker and shopper makes it a two-level channel.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — C。** 生产者与购物者之间经过两个中间环节（批发商和零售商），因此属于二级渠道。

segments.src: **2 — False.** Cross-docking does the opposite: it minimizes storage by moving freight from inbound to outbound trucks within hours, trading inventory buffer for speed and lower holding cost.
segments.tr: **2 — 错误。** 越库作业恰恰相反：它通过在数小时内将货物从入库卡车直接转到出库卡车，把存储降到最低，以库存缓冲换取速度和更低的持有成本。

segments.src: **3 — C.** Picking a single unit means the most labor touches per item plus a dedicated parcel delivery to one address, so its cost per unit is far above pallet or case movement.*
segments.tr: **3 — C。** 拣选单件商品意味着每件商品需要的人工操作最多，还要专门把包裹送到某一个地址，因此单件成本远高于整托盘或整箱的运输。*

segments.tr: - **वितरण केंद्र (DC)** *रीप्लेनिशमेंट* (भरपाई) के लिए बनाया जाता है। ट्रक पैलेट लेकर आते हैं, और ट्रक पैलेट और केस लेकर स्टोरों की ओर निकलते हैं। बड़े दरवाज़े, बड़े उपकरण, प्रति वस्तु कुछ ही बार छूना। कुछ DC में लगभग कुछ भी स्टोर नहीं होता — **क्रॉस-डॉकिंग** में आने वाला माल घंटों के भीतर छाँटकर जाने वाले ट्रकों में फिर से लोड कर दिया जाता है।

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - **फुलफिलमेंट सेंटर (FC)** *ऑर्डर* के लिए बनाया जाता है। यह केस प्राप्त करता है, पर हज़ारों अलग-अलग पतों तक एक-एक इकाई भेजता है। इसे घनी छोटी-वस्तु स्टोरेज, पिक पाथ, पैकिंग स्टेशन, बॉक्स चुनने की व्यवस्था, लेबल प्रिंटर और रिटर्न डेस्क चाहिए। प्रति वस्तु कई बार छूना पड़ता है।

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: **फुलफिलमेंट** उस पूरे ऑर्डर-पक्ष के क्रम का नाम है: प्राप्त करना → स्टोर करना → चुनना → पैक करना → भेजना → रिटर्न संभालना।

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: कंपनियाँ इसे या तो खुद बनाती हैं या **3PL** (थर्ड-पार्टी लॉजिस्टिक्स प्रदाता) से किराये पर लेती हैं — एक बाहरी फ़र्म जो शुल्क लेकर आपका इन्वेंटरी स्टोर करती है और आपके ऑर्डर भेजती है, ताकि आपको वेयरहाउस का लीज़ साइन न करना पड़े।

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: आज ज़्यादातर ब्रांड **ओम्निचैनल** चलाते हैं — एक साथ कई चैनल।

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: इससे एक सचमुच कठिन समस्या पैदा होती है: इन्वेंटरी का एक ही भंडार, मांग की कई धाराएँ।

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: अगर आप अपनी वेबसाइट और किसी स्टोर पर एक ही समय पर आखिरी यूनिट बेच दें, तो किसी का ऑर्डर रद्द हो जाएगा।

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: इससे चतुर समाधान भी निकलते हैं, जैसे **ship-from-store** (सबसे नज़दीकी स्टोर एक छोटा FC बन जाता है) और **BOPIS** — ऑनलाइन खरीदें, स्टोर से उठाएँ — जो महंगे लास्ट-माइल का बोझ ग्राहक की अपनी कार यात्रा पर डाल देता है।
## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Say you run a candle company in Portland, Oregon.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप ओरेगन के पोर्टलैंड में कैंडल कंपनी चलाते हैं।

segments.src: One product, one factory, three channels.
segments.tr: एक उत्पाद, एक फ़ैक्ट्री, तीन चैनल।

segments.src: Watch what happens to the logistics.
segments.tr: देखिए लॉजिस्टिक्स के साथ क्या होता है।

segments.src: **Channel 1 — Target.** You sell wholesale at about $6 a unit.
segments.tr: **चैनल 1 — Target।** आप लगभग $6 प्रति यूनिट पर थोक में बेचते हैं।

segments.src: You palletize, book a truck, and deliver to a Target regional distribution center; Target moves it to stores from there.
segments.tr: आप पैलेट बनाते हैं, ट्रक बुक करते हैं, और Target के क्षेत्रीय वितरण केंद्र पर माल पहुँचाते हैं; Target वहाँ से इसे स्टोरों तक पहुँचाता है।

segments.src: Your per-unit logistics cost is pennies to a few dimes, because you touched pallets, not candles.
segments.tr: आपकी प्रति-यूनिट लॉजिस्टिक्स लागत कुछ पैसे से लेकर कुछ दस-पैसे तक है, क्योंकि आपने कैंडल नहीं, पैलेट छुए।

segments.src: The trade-off: thin margin, strict delivery windows and labeling rules, and you never learn who the buyer is.
segments.tr: ट्रेड-ऑफ़: पतला मार्जिन, सख्त डिलीवरी समय-सीमा और लेबलिंग नियम, और आप कभी नहीं जान पाते कि खरीदार कौन है।

segments.src: **Channel 2 — your own Shopify store.** You sell at $28.
segments.tr: **चैनल 2 — आपका अपना Shopify स्टोर।** आप $28 पर बेचते हैं।
अब *आप* ही फुलफिलमेंट सेंटर हैं।

segments.src: Someone in Cleveland orders one candle.
segments.tr: Cleveland का कोई व्यक्ति एक कैंडल ऑर्डर करता है।
उदाहरण के तौर पर:
pick + pack labor      ~$2-3
box + dunnage          ~$1
parcel shipping        ~$8-10  (2 lb, cross-country, residential)
per-order cost         ~$11-14

segments.src: Then add returns and damage — modest for a candle, but in categories like apparel commonly 20–30% of online orders — with each one needing an inspection, a restock, and a refund.
segments.tr: फिर रिटर्न और क्षति जोड़िए — कैंडल के लिए मामूली, पर apparel जैसी श्रेणियों में ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर का आम तौर पर 20–30% — और हर एक के लिए जाँच, दोबारा स्टॉक और रिफ़ंड करना पड़ता है।

segments.src: Great margin on paper, far less after the box leaves.
segments.tr: कागज़ पर बढ़िया मार्जिन, पर बॉक्स बाहर निकलने के बाद बहुत कम बचता है।

segments.src: **Channel 3 — Amazon.** You ship cases to an Amazon FC in, say, Ontario, California, and Amazon picks, packs, and ships each order.
segments.tr: **चैनल 3 — Amazon।** आप केस को, मान लीजिए, Ontario, California के एक Amazon FC तक भेजते हैं, और Amazon हर ऑर्डर चुनता, पैक करता और भेजता है।

segments.src: You pay a per-unit fulfillment fee (a few dollars for a small, light item), monthly storage, and a referral fee that's commonly around 15% of the sale price in many categories.
segments.tr: आप प्रति-यूनिट फुलफिलमेंट शुल्क (छोटी, हल्की वस्तु के लिए कुछ डॉलर), मासिक स्टोरेज, और कई श्रेणियों में आम तौर पर बिक्री मूल्य के लगभग 15% जितना रेफ़रल शुल्क चुकाते हैं।

segments.src: You've rented someone else's fulfillment operation — and inherited their rules about how everything must be boxed, barcoded, and forecast.
segments.tr: आपने किसी और का फुलफिलमेंट संचालन किराये पर लिया है — और उनके नियम भी अपनाए हैं कि सब कुछ कैसे बॉक्स, बारकोड और पूर्वानुमान करना होगा।

segments.src: Notice that the candle never changed.
segments.tr: ध्यान दीजिए कि कैंडल कभी नहीं बदली।

segments.src: The *channel* changed, and the entire logistics design changed with it: truckload vs.
segments.tr: *चैनल* बदला, और उसके साथ पूरा लॉजिस्टिक्स डिज़ाइन भी बदल गया: ट्रकलोड बनाम
पार्सल, पैलेट बनाम
ईचेज़ (एक-एक यूनिट), एक डिलीवरी बनाम
हज़ारों, बिना रिटर्न डेस्क बनाम
एक व्यस्त रिटर्न डेस्क।

segments.src: That's the whole lesson — and it's why the same brand can be profitable in one channel and quietly lose money in another.
segments.tr: यही पूरा सबक है — और इसी वजह से एक ही ब्रांड एक चैनल में मुनाफ़े में हो सकता है और दूसरे में चुपचाप घाटे में।

segments.src: 1. A distribution channel is the path from maker to end user, and each added level changes who holds inventory and who takes the risk.
segments.tr: 1. वितरण चैनल निर्माता से अंतिम उपयोगकर्ता तक का रास्ता है, और हर अतिरिक्त स्तर बदल देता है कि इन्वेंटरी किसके पास है और जोखिम कौन उठाता है।

segments.src: 2. Distribution centers move pallets and cases to stores; fulfillment centers pick single units for individual shoppers, so cost per unit rises sharply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 2. वितरण केंद्र पैलेट और केस स्टोरों तक पहुँचाते हैं; फुलफिलमेंट सेंटर अलग-अलग ग्राहकों के लिए एक-एक यूनिट चुनते हैं, इसलिए हैंडलिंग इकाई छोटी होने पर प्रति यूनिट लागत तेज़ी से बढ़ती है।

segments.src: 3. Running multiple channels at once (omnichannel) means one inventory pool serving several very different cost structures — which is exactly where profit gets made or lost.
segments.tr: 3. एक साथ कई चैनल चलाने (ओम्निचैनल) का मतलब है एक ही इन्वेंटरी भंडार से बहुत अलग लागत-ढाँचों की सेवा करना — और मुनाफ़ा ठीक यहीं बनता या बिगड़ता है।
## ✅ स्व-परीक्षा

segments.src: **1.** A brand sells through a wholesaler, who sells to independent grocery stores, who sell to shoppers.
segments.tr: **1.** एक ब्रांड थोक विक्रेता के ज़रिए बेचता है, जो स्वतंत्र किराना दुकानों को बेचता है, जो खरीदारों को बेचती हैं।
यह कौन-सा चैनल स्तर है?
- A) शून्य-स्तरीय
- B) एक-स्तरीय
- C) दो-स्तरीय
- D) ओम्निचैनल

segments.src: **2.** True or False — Cross-docking is a strategy for storing inventory longer to protect against demand spikes.
segments.tr: **2.** सही या गलत — क्रॉस-डॉकिंग मांग में उछाल से बचाव के लिए इन्वेंटरी को ज़्यादा समय तक स्टोर करने की रणनीति है।

segments.src: **3.** Which of these would you expect to cost the *most per unit shipped*?
segments.tr: **3.** इनमें से कौन-सा *प्रति भेजी गई यूनिट* सबसे ज़्यादा महंगा पड़ने की उम्मीद करेंगे?

segments.src: - A) Delivering full pallets to a retailer's regional DC
segments.tr: - A) खुदरा विक्रेता के क्षेत्रीय DC तक पूरे पैलेट पहुँचाना

segments.src: - B) Shipping cases to a retailer's store
segments.tr: - B) खुदरा विक्रेता के स्टोर तक केस भेजना

segments.src: - C) Picking and parcel-shipping one item to a customer's home
segments.tr: - C) किसी ग्राहक के घर तक एक वस्तु चुनना और पार्सल से भेजना

segments.src: - D) All three cost about the same per unit
segments.tr: - D) तीनों की प्रति यूनिट लागत लगभग बराबर है
## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The route a product takes from producer to end customer, including any wholesalers, retailers, or marketplaces along the way.
segments.tr: - **वितरण चैनल** — वह रास्ता जिससे कोई उत्पाद निर्माता से अंतिम ग्राहक तक जाता है, बीच में आने वाले थोक विक्रेताओं, खुदरा विक्रेताओं या मार्केटप्लेस सहित।

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC)** — A facility that receives bulk freight and replenishes stores or other DCs, mostly handling pallets and cases.
segments.tr: - **वितरण केंद्र (DC)** — वह सुविधा जो थोक माल प्राप्त करती है और स्टोरों या अन्य DC की भरपाई करती है, मुख्य रूप से पैलेट और केस संभालते हुए।

segments.src: - **Fulfillment center (FC)** — A facility built to pick, pack, and ship individual customer orders, handling single units and returns.
segments.tr: - **फुलफिलमेंट सेंटर (FC)** — वह सुविधा जो व्यक्तिगत ग्राहक ऑर्डर चुनने, पैक करने और भेजने के लिए बनी है, जो एक-एक यूनिट और रिटर्न संभालती है।

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — Sorting inbound freight straight onto outbound trucks with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **क्रॉस-डॉकिंग** — आने वाले माल को बीच में बहुत कम या बिना स्टोरेज के सीधे जाने वाले ट्रकों पर छाँटना।

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics provider)** — An outside company you hire to warehouse inventory and fulfill orders on your behalf.
segments.tr: - **3PL (थर्ड-पार्टी लॉजिस्टिक्स प्रदाता)** — एक बाहरी कंपनी जिसे आप अपनी ओर से इन्वेंटरी वेयरहाउस करने और ऑर्डर पूरे करने के लिए किराये पर लेते हैं।

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Selling through several channels at once (store, website, marketplace, pickup) while trying to serve them from one inventory pool.
segments.tr: - **ओम्निचैनल** — एक साथ कई चैनलों (स्टोर, वेबसाइट, मार्केटप्लेस, पिकअप) से बेचना, और यह कोशिश करना कि सबको एक ही इन्वेंटरी भंडार से सेवा दी जाए।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Two middle stops (wholesaler and retailer) between maker and shopper makes it a two-level channel.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1 — C.** निर्माता और खरीदार के बीच दो बीच के पड़ाव (थोक विक्रेता और खुदरा विक्रेता) इसे दो-स्तरीय चैनल बनाते हैं।

segments.src: **2 — False.** Cross-docking does the opposite: it minimizes storage by moving freight from inbound to outbound trucks within hours, trading inventory buffer for speed and lower holding cost.
segments.tr: **2 — गलत।** क्रॉस-डॉकिंग इसका उल्टा करती है: यह माल को आने वाले ट्रकों से जाने वाले ट्रकों तक घंटों के भीतर ले जाकर स्टोरेज को न्यूनतम रखती है, और इन्वेंटरी के बफ़र के बदले गति और कम होल्डिंग लागत लेती है।

segments.src: **3 — C.** Picking a single unit means the most labor touches per item plus a dedicated parcel delivery to one address, so its cost per unit is far above pallet or case movement.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** एक इकाई चुनने का मतलब है प्रति वस्तु सबसे अधिक श्रम-स्पर्श, और एक पते तक समर्पित पार्सल डिलीवरी, इसलिए इसकी प्रति-यूनिट लागत पैलेट या केस की आवाजाही से कहीं ज़्यादा है।*

es.title: [Logística 101 #10] ¿Por qué enviar una sola vela cuesta más que enviar mil?

segments.src: > The route a product takes to reach you — the distribution channel — decides what kind of warehouse it has to pass through, and that decision drives most of the shipping cost you never see on the price tag.
segments.tr: > La ruta que recorre un producto hasta llegar a ti (el canal de distribución) determina por qué tipo de almacén debe pasar, y esa decisión explica la mayor parte del costo de envío que nunca ves en la etiqueta del precio.
## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: A **distribution channel** is simply the path a product travels from the company that makes it to the person who uses it.
segments.tr: Un **canal de distribución** es simplemente la ruta que recorre un producto desde la empresa que lo fabrica hasta la persona que lo usa.

segments.src: Channels are usually described by how many middle stops they contain:
segments.tr: Los canales suelen describirse según cuántas paradas intermedias tienen:

segments.src: - **Zero-level (direct-to-consumer):** maker → you. A brand's own website.
segments.tr: - **Nivel cero (directo al consumidor):** fabricante → tú. El sitio web propio de una marca.

segments.src: - **One-level:** maker → retailer → you. A jar of salsa sold at Kroger.
segments.tr: - **Un nivel:** fabricante → minorista → tú. Un frasco de salsa vendido en Kroger.

segments.src: - **Two-level:** maker → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you. How most small hardware stores and restaurants get supplied.
segments.tr: - **Dos niveles:** fabricante → mayorista/distribuidor → minorista → tú. Así es como se abastecen la mayoría de las pequeñas ferreterías y restaurantes.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: the channel isn't just a sales decision.
segments.tr: Aquí está la parte que sorprende a la gente: el canal no es solo una decisión de ventas.

segments.src: It quietly dictates your *logistics*, because each channel hands off goods in a different **unit of handling**.
segments.tr: Silenciosamente determina tu *logística*, porque cada canal entrega las mercancías en una **unidad de manejo** distinta.
Piensa en tres tamaños:
pallet  →  case  →  each (one single unit)
Una tarima (pallet) puede contener 40 cajas.
Una caja puede contener 12 velas.

segments.src: Moving one pallet takes a forklift driver about a minute.
segments.tr: Mover una tarima le toma a un operador de montacargas alrededor de un minuto.

segments.src: Picking, packing, labeling, and shipping *one* candle takes a person a few minutes and a box, and then a parcel carrier charges you for a separate delivery to a separate house.
segments.tr: Preparar, empacar, etiquetar y enviar *una* vela le toma a una persona unos minutos y una caja, y luego una empresa de paquetería te cobra por una entrega separada a una casa distinta.

segments.src: That's why the cost per unit climbs steeply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: Por eso el costo por unidad sube drásticamente a medida que la unidad de manejo se reduce.

segments.src: Same product, same warehouse racks — completely different economics.
segments.tr: Mismo producto, mismos estantes de almacén: economía completamente distinta.

segments.src: This split shows up in the buildings themselves:
segments.tr: Esta diferencia se refleja en los propios edificios:

segments.src: - A **distribution center (DC)** is built for *replenishment*. Trucks arrive with pallets, and trucks leave with pallets and cases headed to stores. Big doors, big equipment, few touches per item. Some DCs barely store anything at all — in **cross-docking**, inbound freight is sorted and reloaded onto outbound trucks within hours.
segments.tr: - Un **centro de distribución (DC)** está diseñado para *reabastecimiento*. Los camiones llegan con tarimas y salen con tarimas y cajas dirigidas a tiendas. Puertas grandes, equipo grande, pocas manipulaciones por artículo. Algunos centros de distribución casi no almacenan nada: en el **cross-docking**, la mercancía entrante se clasifica y se recarga en camiones salientes en cuestión de horas.

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - Un **centro de cumplimiento (FC)** está diseñado para *pedidos*. Recibe cajas, pero envía unidades individuales a miles de direcciones distintas. Necesita almacenamiento denso de artículos pequeños, rutas de preparación, estaciones de empaque, selección de cajas, impresoras de etiquetas y un mostrador de devoluciones. Muchas manipulaciones por artículo.

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: **Cumplimiento de pedidos (fulfillment)** es el nombre de toda esa secuencia del lado de los pedidos: recibir → almacenar → preparar (picking) → empacar → enviar → gestionar devoluciones.

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: Las empresas lo construyen ellas mismas o lo contratan a un **3PL** (proveedor externo de logística): una firma externa que almacena tu inventario y envía tus pedidos a cambio de una tarifa, para que no tengas que firmar un contrato de arrendamiento de almacén.

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: Hoy en día, la mayoría de las marcas operan en **omnicanal**: varios canales a la vez.

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: Eso crea un problema realmente difícil: un solo inventario, muchas fuentes de demanda.

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: Vende la última unidad en tu sitio web y en una tienda al mismo tiempo, y alguien verá su pedido cancelado.

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: También surgen soluciones ingeniosas, como **ship-from-store** (la tienda más cercana funciona como un mini centro de cumplimiento) y **BOPIS** (buy online, pick up in store: compra en línea, recoge en tienda), que traslada la costosa última milla al viaje en auto del propio cliente.
## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you run a candle company in Portland, Oregon.
segments.tr: Supongamos que diriges una empresa de velas en Portland, Oregón.

segments.src: One product, one factory, three channels.
segments.tr: Un producto, una fábrica, tres canales.

segments.src: Watch what happens to the logistics.
segments.tr: Observa qué pasa con la logística.

segments.src: **Channel 1 — Target.** You sell wholesale at about $6 a unit.
segments.tr: **Canal 1: Target.** Vendes al por mayor a unos $6 por unidad.

segments.src: You palletize, book a truck, and deliver to a Target regional distribution center; Target moves it to stores from there.
segments.tr: Paletizas, reservas un camión y entregas en un centro de distribución regional de Target; desde allí, Target lo lleva a las tiendas.

segments.src: Your per-unit logistics cost is pennies to a few dimes, because you touched pallets, not candles.
segments.tr: Tu costo logístico por unidad es de unos centavos a unas pocas décimas de dólar, porque manipulaste tarimas, no velas.

segments.src: The trade-off: thin margin, strict delivery windows and labeling rules, and you never learn who the buyer is.
segments.tr: La contrapartida: margen estrecho, ventanas de entrega y reglas de etiquetado estrictas, y nunca sabes quién es el comprador.

segments.src: **Channel 2 — your own Shopify store.** You sell at $28.
segments.tr: **Canal 2: tu propia tienda en Shopify.** Vendes a $28.
Ahora *tú* eres el centro de cumplimiento.

segments.src: Someone in Cleveland orders one candle.
segments.tr: Alguien en Cleveland pide una vela.
A modo ilustrativo:
pick + pack labor      ~$2-3
box + dunnage          ~$1
parcel shipping        ~$8-10  (2 lb, cross-country, residential)
per-order cost         ~$11-14

segments.src: Then add returns and damage — modest for a candle, but in categories like apparel commonly 20–30% of online orders — with each one needing an inspection, a restock, and a refund.
segments.tr: Luego suma las devoluciones y los daños: modestos en una vela, pero en categorías como la ropa suelen representar entre el 20 % y el 30 % de los pedidos en línea, y cada una requiere inspección, reposición y reembolso.

segments.src: Great margin on paper, far less after the box leaves.
segments.tr: Gran margen en papel, mucho menos después de que la caja sale.

segments.src: **Channel 3 — Amazon.** You ship cases to an Amazon FC in, say, Ontario, California, and Amazon picks, packs, and ships each order.
segments.tr: **Canal 3: Amazon.** Envías cajas a un centro de cumplimiento de Amazon en, digamos, Ontario, California, y Amazon prepara, empaca y envía cada pedido.

segments.src: You pay a per-unit fulfillment fee (a few dollars for a small, light item), monthly storage, and a referral fee that's commonly around 15% of the sale price in many categories.
segments.tr: Pagas una tarifa de cumplimiento por unidad (unos cuantos dólares por un artículo pequeño y ligero), almacenamiento mensual y una comisión por referencia que suele rondar el 15 % del precio de venta en muchas categorías.

segments.src: You've rented someone else's fulfillment operation — and inherited their rules about how everything must be boxed, barcoded, and forecast.
segments.tr: Has contratado la operación de cumplimiento de otro, y heredas sus reglas sobre cómo debe empaquetarse, codificarse con código de barras y pronosticarse todo.

segments.src: Notice that the candle never changed.
segments.tr: Fíjate en que la vela nunca cambió.

segments.src: The *channel* changed, and the entire logistics design changed with it: truckload vs.
segments.tr: Cambió el *canal*, y con él cambió todo el diseño logístico: carga completa de camión vs.
envío por paquetería; tarimas vs.
unidades sueltas; una entrega vs.
miles; sin mostrador de devoluciones vs.
uno muy ocupado.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson — and it's why the same brand can be profitable in one channel and quietly lose money in another.
segments.tr: Esa es toda la lección, y por eso la misma marca puede ser rentable en un canal y perder dinero discretamente en otro.
## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. A distribution channel is the path from maker to end user, and each added level changes who holds inventory and who takes the risk.
segments.tr: 1. Un canal de distribución es la ruta del fabricante al usuario final, y cada nivel adicional cambia quién mantiene el inventario y quién asume el riesgo.

segments.src: 2. Distribution centers move pallets and cases to stores; fulfillment centers pick single units for individual shoppers, so cost per unit rises sharply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 2. Los centros de distribución mueven tarimas y cajas hacia las tiendas; los centros de cumplimiento preparan unidades individuales para compradores específicos, así que el costo por unidad sube bruscamente a medida que la unidad de manejo se reduce.

segments.src: 3. Running multiple channels at once (omnichannel) means one inventory pool serving several very different cost structures — which is exactly where profit gets made or lost.
segments.tr: 3. Operar varios canales a la vez (omnicanal) significa que un solo inventario atiende varias estructuras de costos muy distintas, que es exactamente donde se gana o se pierde dinero.
## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** A brand sells through a wholesaler, who sells to independent grocery stores, who sell to shoppers.
segments.tr: **1.** Una marca vende a través de un mayorista, que vende a tiendas de abarrotes independientes, que venden a compradores.
¿De qué nivel de canal se trata?
- A) Nivel cero
- B) Un nivel
- C) Dos niveles
- D) Omnicanal

segments.src: **2.** True or False — Cross-docking is a strategy for storing inventory longer to protect against demand spikes.
segments.tr: **2.** Verdadero o falso: el cross-docking es una estrategia para almacenar inventario durante más tiempo y protegerse contra picos de demanda.

segments.src: **3.** Which of these would you expect to cost the *most per unit shipped*?
segments.tr: **3.** ¿Cuál de estas opciones esperarías que cueste *más por unidad enviada*?

segments.src: - A) Delivering full pallets to a retailer's regional DC
segments.tr: - A) Entregar tarimas completas al centro de distribución regional de un minorista

segments.src: - B) Shipping cases to a retailer's store
segments.tr: - B) Enviar cajas a una tienda del minorista

segments.src: - C) Picking and parcel-shipping one item to a customer's home
segments.tr: - C) Preparar y enviar por paquetería un solo artículo al domicilio de un cliente

segments.src: - D) All three cost about the same per unit
segments.tr: - D) Las tres cuestan más o menos lo mismo por unidad
## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The route a product takes from producer to end customer, including any wholesalers, retailers, or marketplaces along the way.
segments.tr: - **Canal de distribución**: la ruta que sigue un producto desde el productor hasta el cliente final, incluidos los mayoristas, minoristas o mercados en el camino.

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC)** — A facility that receives bulk freight and replenishes stores or other DCs, mostly handling pallets and cases.
segments.tr: - **Centro de distribución (DC)**: instalación que recibe carga a granel y reabastece tiendas u otros centros de distribución, manejando principalmente tarimas y cajas.

segments.src: - **Fulfillment center (FC)** — A facility built to pick, pack, and ship individual customer orders, handling single units and returns.
segments.tr: - **Centro de cumplimiento (FC)**: instalación diseñada para preparar, empacar y enviar pedidos individuales de clientes, manejando unidades sueltas y devoluciones.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — Sorting inbound freight straight onto outbound trucks with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking**: clasificar la carga entrante directamente en camiones salientes, con poco o ningún almacenamiento intermedio.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics provider)** — An outside company you hire to warehouse inventory and fulfill orders on your behalf.
segments.tr: - **3PL (proveedor externo de logística)**: empresa externa que contratas para almacenar inventario y cumplir pedidos en tu nombre.

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Selling through several channels at once (store, website, marketplace, pickup) while trying to serve them from one inventory pool.
segments.tr: - **Omnicanal**: vender a través de varios canales a la vez (tienda, sitio web, mercado en línea, recogida) intentando atenderlos desde un solo inventario.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Two middle stops (wholesaler and retailer) between maker and shopper makes it a two-level channel.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — C.** Dos paradas intermedias (mayorista y minorista) entre el fabricante y el comprador hacen que sea un canal de dos niveles.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Cross-docking does the opposite: it minimizes storage by moving freight from inbound to outbound trucks within hours, trading inventory buffer for speed and lower holding cost.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** El cross-docking hace lo contrario: minimiza el almacenamiento al mover la carga de camiones entrantes a salientes en cuestión de horas, a cambio de un colchón de inventario por velocidad y menor costo de mantenimiento.

segments.src: **3 — C.** Picking a single unit means the most labor touches per item plus a dedicated parcel delivery to one address, so its cost per unit is far above pallet or case movement.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** Preparar un solo artículo implica la mayor cantidad de mano de obra por artículo más una entrega dedicada por paquetería a una sola dirección, así que su costo por unidad está muy por encima del de mover tarimas o cajas.*

ar.title: [Logistics 101 #10] لماذا تكلّف شحن شمعة واحدة أكثر من شحن ألف شمعة

segments.src: > The route a product takes to reach you — the distribution channel — decides what kind of warehouse it has to pass through, and that decision drives most of the shipping cost you never see on the price tag.
segments.tr: > قناة التوزيع — المسار الذي يسلكه المنتج ليصل إليك — هي التي تحدد نوع المستودع الذي يجب أن يمر به، وهذا القرار يقود معظم تكلفة الشحن التي لا تراها على بطاقة السعر.
## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: A **distribution channel** is simply the path a product travels from the company that makes it to the person who uses it.
segments.tr: **قناة التوزيع** هي ببساطة المسار الذي تسلكه السلعة من الشركة التي تصنعها إلى الشخص الذي يستخدمها.

segments.src: Channels are usually described by how many middle stops they contain:
segments.tr: تُوصف القنوات عادةً بعدد المحطات الوسيطة التي تتضمنها:

segments.src: - **Zero-level (direct-to-consumer):** maker → you. A brand's own website.
segments.tr: - **المستوى الصفري (من المصنع إلى المستهلك مباشرة):** الصانع ← أنت. موقع الإلكتروني الخاص بالعلامة التجارية.

segments.src: - **One-level:** maker → retailer → you. A jar of salsa sold at Kroger.
segments.tr: - **مستوى واحد:** الصانع ← تاجر التجزئة ← أنت. عبوة صلصة سالسا تُباع في Kroger.

segments.src: - **Two-level:** maker → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you. How most small hardware stores and restaurants get supplied.
segments.tr: - **مستويان:** الصانع ← تاجر الجملة/الموزع ← تاجر التجزئة ← أنت. هكذا يتم تزويد معظم متاجر الأدوات المنزلية الصغيرة والمطاعم.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: the channel isn't just a sales decision.
segments.tr: وهنا الجزء الذي يفاجئ الناس: القناة ليست مجرد قرار بيع.

segments.src: It quietly dictates your *logistics*, because each channel hands off goods in a different **unit of handling**.
segments.tr: بل هي تحدد *لوجستيّاتك* بهدوء، لأن كل قناة تسلّم البضائع بـ**وحدة مناولة** مختلفة.
تخيّل ثلاثة أحجام:
pallet  →  case  →  each (one single unit)
قد تحتوي الطبلية (البالتة) على 40 صندوقاً.
وقد يحتوي الصندوق على 12 شمعة.

segments.src: Moving one pallet takes a forklift driver about a minute.
segments.tr: ونقل طبلية واحدة يستغرق من سائق الرافعة الشوكية نحو دقيقة.

segments.src: Picking, packing, labeling, and shipping *one* candle takes a person a few minutes and a box, and then a parcel carrier charges you for a separate delivery to a separate house.
segments.tr: أما التقاط شمعة *واحدة* وتعبئتها وتغليفها ووضع ملصق عليها وشحنها فيستغرق من شخص بضع دقائق وصندوقاً، ثم تتقاضى شركة الشحن منك رسوماً مقابل توصيل منفصل إلى منزل منفصل.

segments.src: That's why the cost per unit climbs steeply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: لهذا ترتفع تكلفة الوحدة بشكل حاد كلما صغُر حجم وحدة المناولة.

segments.src: Same product, same warehouse racks — completely different economics.
segments.tr: المنتج نفسه، ونفس أرفف المستودع — لكن اقتصاديات مختلفة تماماً.

segments.src: This split shows up in the buildings themselves:
segments.tr: ينعكس هذا الفرق في المباني نفسها:

segments.src: - A **distribution center (DC)** is built for *replenishment*. Trucks arrive with pallets, and trucks leave with pallets and cases headed to stores. Big doors, big equipment, few touches per item. Some DCs barely store anything at all — in **cross-docking**, inbound freight is sorted and reloaded onto outbound trucks within hours.
segments.tr: - **مركز التوزيع (DC)** مصمم لـ*إعادة التزويد*. تصل الشاحنات محمّلة بالطبليات، وتغادر محمّلة بالطبليات والصناديق المتجهة إلى المتاجر. أبواب كبيرة، معدات كبيرة، قليل من اللمسات لكل صنف. بعض مراكز التوزيع لا تخزّن شيئاً تقريباً — ففي **الربط العابر (cross-docking)** تُفرز البضائع الواردة وتُعاد تحميلها على شاحنات الصادر خلال ساعات.

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - **مركز التنفيذ (FC)** مصمم لـ*الطلبات*. يستلم الصناديق لكنه يشحن وحدات مفردة إلى آلاف العناوين الفردية. يحتاج إلى تخزين كثيف للأصناف الصغيرة، ومسارات التقاط، ومحطات تعبئة، واختيار للصناديق، وطابعات ملصقات، ومكتب للمرتجعات. لمسات كثيرة لكل صنف.

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: **التنفيذ (Fulfillment)** هو الاسم الذي يطلق على تسلسل الطلبات بأكمله: الاستلام ← التخزين ← الالتقاط ← التعبئة ← الشحن ← معالجة المرتجعات.

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: تقوم الشركات إما ببنائه بنفسها أو تستأجره من **3PL** (مزود الخدمات اللوجستية من الطرف الثالث) — وهي شركة خارجية تخزّن مخزونك وتشحن طلباتك مقابل رسوم، فلا تحتاج إلى توقيع عقد إيجار لمستودع.

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: معظم العلامات التجارية اليوم تعمل بنظام **متعدد القنوات (omnichannel)** — عدة قنوات في آنٍ واحد.

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: وهذا يخلق مشكلة صعبة فعلاً: مجموعة واحدة من المخزون، وتدفقات طلب كثيرة.

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: بِع آخر قطعة على موقعك وفي متجر في اللحظة نفسها، وسيُلغى طلب أحد الزبائن.

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: وهو يولّد أيضاً حلولاً ذكية، مثل **الشحن من المتجر (ship-from-store)** حيث يصبح أقرب متجر بمثابة مركز تنفيذ مصغّر، و**BOPIS** — اشترِ عبر الإنترنت واستلم من المتجر — الذي ينقل مرحلة الميل الأخير المكلفة إلى رحلة السيارة الخاصة بالزبون.

fr.title: [Logistics 101 #10] Pourquoi expédier une seule bougie coûte plus cher qu'en expédier mille

segments.src: > The route a product takes to reach you — the distribution channel — decides what kind of warehouse it has to pass through, and that decision drives most of the shipping cost you never see on the price tag.
segments.tr: > La route qu'emprunte un produit pour arriver jusqu'à vous (le canal de distribution) détermine le type d'entrepôt qu'il doit traverser, et cette décision conditionne l'essentiel des coûts d'expédition que vous ne voyez jamais sur l'étiquette de prix.
## Concept du jour

segments.src: A **distribution channel** is simply the path a product travels from the company that makes it to the person who uses it.
segments.tr: Un **canal de distribution** est simplement le chemin parcouru par un produit depuis l'entreprise qui le fabrique jusqu'à la personne qui l'utilise.

segments.src: Channels are usually described by how many middle stops they contain:
segments.tr: Les canaux se décrivent généralement par le nombre d'intermédiaires qu'ils comportent :

segments.src: - **Zero-level (direct-to-consumer):** maker → you. A brand's own website.
segments.tr: - **Niveau zéro (vente directe au consommateur) :** fabricant → vous. Le site web propre à une marque.

segments.src: - **One-level:** maker → retailer → you. A jar of salsa sold at Kroger.
segments.tr: - **Un niveau :** fabricant → détaillant → vous. Un pot de salsa vendu chez Kroger.

segments.src: - **Two-level:** maker → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you. How most small hardware stores and restaurants get supplied.
segments.tr: - **Deux niveaux :** fabricant → grossiste/distributeur → détaillant → vous. C'est ainsi que la plupart des petites quincailleries et restaurants s'approvisionnent.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: the channel isn't just a sales decision.
segments.tr: Voici ce qui surprend la plupart des gens : le canal n'est pas seulement une décision commerciale.

segments.src: It quietly dictates your *logistics*, because each channel hands off goods in a different **unit of handling**.
segments.tr: Il dicte discrètement votre *logistique*, car chaque canal transmet les marchandises selon une **unité de manutention** différente.
Imaginez trois tailles :
pallet  →  case  →  each (one single unit)
Une palette peut contenir 40 cartons.
Un carton peut contenir 12 bougies.

segments.src: Moving one pallet takes a forklift driver about a minute.
segments.tr: Déplacer une palette prend à un cariste environ une minute.

segments.src: Picking, packing, labeling, and shipping *one* candle takes a person a few minutes and a box, and then a parcel carrier charges you for a separate delivery to a separate house.
segments.tr: Préparer, emballer, étiqueter et expédier *une* bougie demande à une personne quelques minutes et un colis, puis un transporteur facture une livraison distincte à une adresse distincte.

segments.src: That's why the cost per unit climbs steeply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi le coût unitaire grimpe fortement à mesure que l'unité de manutention rétrécit.

segments.src: Same product, same warehouse racks — completely different economics.
segments.tr: Même produit, mêmes rayonnages d'entrepôt, économie totalement différente.

segments.src: This split shows up in the buildings themselves:
segments.tr: Cette division se retrouve dans les bâtiments eux-mêmes :

segments.src: - A **distribution center (DC)** is built for *replenishment*. Trucks arrive with pallets, and trucks leave with pallets and cases headed to stores. Big doors, big equipment, few touches per item. Some DCs barely store anything at all — in **cross-docking**, inbound freight is sorted and reloaded onto outbound trucks within hours.
segments.tr: - Un **centre de distribution (DC)** est conçu pour le *réassortiment*. Les camions arrivent avec des palettes et repartent avec des palettes et des cartons à destination des magasins. Grandes portes, gros équipements, peu de manipulations par article. Certains DC ne stockent presque rien : dans le **cross-docking**, les marchandises entrantes sont triées et rechargées sur des camions sortants en quelques heures.

segments.src: - A **fulfillment center (FC)** is built for *orders*. It receives cases but ships single units to thousands of individual addresses. It needs dense small-item storage, pick paths, packing stations, box selection, label printers, and a returns desk. Many touches per item.
segments.tr: - Un **centre d'exécution des commandes (FC)** est conçu pour les *commandes*. Il reçoit des cartons mais expédie des unités individuelles vers des milliers d'adresses distinctes. Il lui faut un stockage dense de petits articles, des circuits de préparation, des postes d'emballage, la sélection des cartons, des imprimantes d'étiquettes et un comptoir de retours. Beaucoup de manipulations par article.

segments.src: **Fulfillment** is the name for that whole order-side sequence: receive → store → pick → pack → ship → handle returns.
segments.tr: L'**exécution des commandes** (fulfillment) désigne l'ensemble de cette séquence côté commandes : réception → stockage → préparation → emballage → expédition → gestion des retours.

segments.src: Companies either build it themselves or rent it from a **3PL** (third-party logistics provider) — an outside firm that stores your inventory and ships your orders for a fee, so you don't have to sign a warehouse lease.
segments.tr: Les entreprises la réalisent soit elles-mêmes, soit la sous-traitent à un **3PL** (prestataire logistique tiers), c'est-à-dire une société externe qui stocke votre inventaire et expédie vos commandes contre rémunération, sans que vous ayez à signer un bail d'entrepôt.

segments.src: Most brands today run **omnichannel** — several channels at once.
segments.tr: La plupart des marques pratiquent aujourd'hui l'**omnicanal**, c'est-à-dire plusieurs canaux à la fois.

segments.src: That creates a genuinely hard problem: one pool of inventory, many demand streams.
segments.tr: Cela crée un problème réellement difficile : un seul stock, plusieurs flux de demande.

segments.src: Sell the last unit on your website and in a store at the same moment, and someone's order gets canceled.
segments.tr: Vendez la dernière unité sur votre site et en magasin au même moment, et la commande de quelqu'un sera annulée.

segments.src: It also creates clever fixes, like **ship-from-store** (the nearest store becomes a mini-FC) and **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store — which shifts the expensive last mile onto the customer's own car trip.
segments.tr: Cela fait aussi naître des solutions astucieuses, comme le **ship-from-store** (le magasin le plus proche devient un mini-FC) et le **BOPIS** (buy online, pick up in store : acheter en ligne, retirer en magasin), qui reporte le coûteux dernier kilomètre sur le trajet en voiture du client lui-même.
## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: Say you run a candle company in Portland, Oregon.
segments.tr: Imaginons que vous dirigiez une entreprise de bougies à Portland, dans l'Oregon.

segments.src: One product, one factory, three channels.
segments.tr: Un produit, une usine, trois canaux.

segments.src: Watch what happens to the logistics.
segments.tr: Voyez ce qui se passe pour la logistique.

segments.src: **Channel 1 — Target.** You sell wholesale at about $6 a unit.
segments.tr: **Canal 1 : Target.** Vous vendez en gros à environ 6 $ l'unité.

segments.src: You palletize, book a truck, and deliver to a Target regional distribution center; Target moves it to stores from there.
segments.tr: Vous palettisez, réservez un camion et livrez un centre de distribution régional de Target ; Target l'achemine ensuite vers ses magasins.

segments.src: Your per-unit logistics cost is pennies to a few dimes, because you touched pallets, not candles.
segments.tr: Votre coût logistique unitaire se chiffre en centimes, voire en quelques dizaines de centimes, car vous manipulez des palettes, pas des bougies.

segments.src: The trade-off: thin margin, strict delivery windows and labeling rules, and you never learn who the buyer is.
segments.tr: Le compromis : une marge faible, des créneaux de livraison et des règles d'étiquetage stricts, et vous ne savez jamais qui est l'acheteur.

segments.src: **Channel 2 — your own Shopify store.** You sell at $28.
segments.tr: **Canal 2 : votre propre boutique Shopify.** Vous vendez à 28 $.
Ici, *vous* êtes le centre d'exécution des commandes.

segments.src: Someone in Cleveland orders one candle.
segments.tr: Quelqu'un à Cleveland commande une bougie.
À titre d'illustration :
pick + pack labor      ~$2-3
box + dunnage          ~$1
parcel shipping        ~$8-10  (2 lb, cross-country, residential)
per-order cost         ~$11-14

segments.src: Then add returns and damage — modest for a candle, but in categories like apparel commonly 20–30% of online orders — with each one needing an inspection, a restock, and a refund.
segments.tr: Ajoutez ensuite les retours et les dommages : modestes pour une bougie, mais dans des catégories comme l'habillement, ils représentent souvent 20 à 30 % des commandes en ligne. Chacun nécessite un contrôle, une remise en stock et un remboursement.

segments.src: Great margin on paper, far less after the box leaves.
segments.tr: Une belle marge sur le papier, bien moindre une fois le colis parti.

segments.src: **Channel 3 — Amazon.** You ship cases to an Amazon FC in, say, Ontario, California, and Amazon picks, packs, and ships each order.
segments.tr: **Canal 3 : Amazon.** Vous expédiez des cartons vers un FC d'Amazon à Ontario, en Californie, par exemple, et Amazon prépare, emballe et expédie chaque commande.

segments.src: You pay a per-unit fulfillment fee (a few dollars for a small, light item), monthly storage, and a referral fee that's commonly around 15% of the sale price in many categories.
segments.tr: Vous payez des frais d'exécution par unité (quelques dollars pour un petit article léger), un stockage mensuel et une commission de référencement qui atteint souvent environ 15 % du prix de vente dans de nombreuses catégories.

segments.src: You've rented someone else's fulfillment operation — and inherited their rules about how everything must be boxed, barcoded, and forecast.
segments.tr: Vous avez loué l'opération logistique d'un autre, et hérité de ses règles sur la façon dont tout doit être emballé, codé-barres et prévu.

segments.src: Notice that the candle never changed.
segments.tr: Remarquez que la bougie n'a jamais changé.

segments.src: The *channel* changed, and the entire logistics design changed with it: truckload vs.
segments.tr: Le *canal* a changé, et toute la conception logistique a suivi : camion complet vs.
colis, palettes vs.
unités, une livraison vs.
des milliers, pas de comptoir de retours vs.
un comptoir très sollicité.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson — and it's why the same brand can be profitable in one channel and quietly lose money in another.
segments.tr: C'est toute la leçon, et la raison pour laquelle une même marque peut être rentable dans un canal et perdre discrètement de l'argent dans un autre.
## Résumé en 3 points

segments.src: 1. A distribution channel is the path from maker to end user, and each added level changes who holds inventory and who takes the risk.
segments.tr: 1. Un canal de distribution est le chemin du fabricant à l'utilisateur final, et chaque niveau ajouté modifie qui détient le stock et qui prend le risque.

segments.src: 2. Distribution centers move pallets and cases to stores; fulfillment centers pick single units for individual shoppers, so cost per unit rises sharply as the handling unit shrinks.
segments.tr: 2. Les centres de distribution déplacent palettes et cartons vers les magasins ; les centres d'exécution prélèvent des unités individuelles pour des acheteurs particuliers, donc le coût unitaire monte nettement à mesure que l'unité de manutention rétrécit.

segments.src: 3. Running multiple channels at once (omnichannel) means one inventory pool serving several very different cost structures — which is exactly where profit gets made or lost.
segments.tr: 3. Gérer plusieurs canaux en même temps (omnicanal) signifie qu'un seul stock alimente des structures de coûts très différentes, et c'est précisément là que se gagne ou se perd le profit.
## ✅ Quiz d'auto-évaluation

segments.src: **1.** A brand sells through a wholesaler, who sells to independent grocery stores, who sell to shoppers.
segments.tr: **1.** Une marque vend par l'intermédiaire d'un grossiste, qui vend à des épiceries indépendantes, qui vendent à des acheteurs.

- C) Deux niveaux
